findings.evidence: src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_evaluation.py, run_stage_e: `if len(sealed_members) != expected:` checks only list length; `sealed_case_id_set = {member["case_id"] for member in sealed_members}` converts the members to a set; and `missing = sorted(sealed_case_id_set - set(labels))` / `extra = sorted(set(labels) - sealed_case_id_set)` compare labels only to that deduplicated set. The loop then increments `eligible += 1` once per list member. No uniqueness check of `member["case_id"]` or validation of the receipt's `listing_witness_digest` occurs in run_stage_e. By contrast, src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_lifecycle.py, assert_prediction_stream_complete contains the required duplicate check: `if duplicates: raise LifecycleError(...)`.
findings.reproduction: Start with a valid rehearsal stream. Replace its last member with a deep copy of member 0, leaving `len(members) == 120`; remove the omitted last case's label; set `receipt["member_count"] = 120`, set `receipt["stream_digest"] = canonical_digest(members)`, and recompute `receipt["receipt_digest"]` exactly as run_stage_e does. Invoke run_stage_e with `existing_result_digests=()`. The deduplicated case-ID set has 119 IDs and exactly matches the 119 labels; the loop nevertheless scores the duplicated case twice, increments `eligible` to 120, and can return PASS.
findings.residual_limitation: Even after Stage E verifies unique IDs, exact membership, and the listing witness, assurance that the receipt and member bytes came from immutable storage still depends on the external sealing and storage boundary.
findings.title: Stage E accepts a 120-member stream with duplicate case IDs and an omitted case

findings.evidence: src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_evaluation.py, create_preregistration_lock enforces prior existence only through `if existing_lock_digest is not None:`. seal_prediction_stream forwards the caller value through `lifecycle.assert_create_only_plan(existing_objects=existing_objects, ...)`. run_stage_e likewise begins `already = sorted({digest for digest in existing_result_digests})` and refuses only under `if already:`. None of these functions records an object, reads an authoritative object listing, or changes persistent ordinal state. src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_lifecycle.py, next_ordinal similarly derives its result solely from supplied state: `if current_ordinal != 0: raise LifecycleError(...)` followed by `return 1`. The supplied test only exercises truthful evidence: tests/test_parser_v3_v2_rehearsal.py states `existing_result_digests=[evaluation.canonical_digest(run["result"])]` in `test_a_second_formal_result_is_refused`.
findings.reproduction: Using otherwise valid lock, receipt, members, labels, and strata, call run_stage_e once with `existing_result_digests=()`. Call it again with the identical arguments and again pass `existing_result_digests=()`. The function performs no mutation on the first call and therefore returns a second formal result on the second call. Similarly, two calls to create_preregistration_lock with identical bindings and `existing_lock_digest=None`, or two calls to seal_prediction_stream with `existing_objects=()`, are both accepted.
findings.residual_limitation: A corrected implementation still requires an authenticated, atomic storage operation or durable ledger outside these pure functions to make existence evidence truthful under concurrent callers.
findings.title: One-shot and create-only controls trust caller-supplied nonexistence evidence

findings.evidence: src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_construction.py defines `TARGET_KEY_FRAGMENTS` as only `"target", "expected", "quota", "must_equal", "required_count", "repairable", "residual_count"`. Its enforcement is restricted to `return any(fragment in lowered for fragment in TARGET_KEY_FRAGMENTS)` and `if under_target_key and node in historical:`. Thus a target key not containing one of those fragments never sets `under_target_key`, even where its values are precisely 105 and 15.
findings.reproduction: Call `assert_split_is_not_a_target({"desired_repair_count": 105, "desired_remaining": 15})`. Neither key contains any registered fragment: in particular, `desired_repair_count` does not contain `repairable`, and neither key contains `target`, `expected`, `quota`, `must_equal`, `required_count`, or `residual_count`. The function returns normally despite the mapping explicitly encoding the prohibited desired 105/15 outcome.
findings.residual_limitation: No key-name heuristic alone can establish that arbitrary future rule structures lack a semantic target; the registered construction representation must make the relevant counts structurally closed and validate them there.
findings.title: The historical 105/15 target guard can be bypassed with unregistered target keys

report.summary: I checked the lifecycle, construction, evaluation, and supplied rehearsal controls. Stage E recomputes its status and rejects ordinary short streams, ineligible labels, mismatched labels, and altered receipts. However, a self-consistent receipt with duplicate members is accepted because Stage E checks only list length and set equality, permitting an effective denominator below 120. The one-shot and create-only guarantees are also caller-asserted rather than persisted: callers can supply empty existence evidence repeatedly. Finally, the historical 105/15-target guard omits ordinary target-like key names and can be bypassed. These paths permit formal results or construction rules contrary to the stated scientific protocol.
